business_problem: HippoScreen needed to improve the efficiency, build times, and clinical robustness of its EEG-based AI diagnostic system so it could search large algorithm combinations faster and deliver mental health diagnostic results to clinicians on time.
solution_summary: HippoScreen's Stress EEG Assessment (SEA) System combines an EEG amplifier, a clinician-facing GUI, and an AI analytics stack to turn 90-second brainwave recordings into an objective depression-risk score. The amplifier collects and preprocesses EEG signals, while the GUI controls the test workflow and presents results to medical staff. In the compute layer, HippoScreen mixes proprietary algorithms with scikit-learn machine-learning methods for feature extraction, feature selection, clustering, classification, and regression, plus PyTorch deep-learning models such as SCCNet, EEGNet, and Shallow ConvNet. Intel VTune Profiler was used to inspect CPU and software thread behavior across Python environments and identify thread oversubscription; HippoScreen then tuned execution to a five-thread sweet spot. Intel Extension for Scikit-learn and Intel Optimization for PyTorch accelerated model build and validation cycles, helping the team test parameter combinations faster and shorten delivery of diagnostic output. The page names no storage product, but it does cite a large cross-center EEG database supporting the broader solution.

data_flow: Patients' 90-second EEG brainwave signals are captured by the EEG amplifier, processed inside the SEA System, and passed through preprocessing, feature extraction, feature selection, and classifier stages implemented with proprietary algorithms, scikit-learn, and PyTorch models. The system then produces a numerical evaluation index representing depression probability for doctors through the GUI.
business_outcome: HippoScreen improved model and workload performance, reduced build times for its EEG diagnostic AI, and could broaden Brain Waves AI applications to more psychiatric conditions and diseases while delivering results to medical personnel faster.
